title: Defense Secretary Hegseth’s Entourage Reprimanded by Guard at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
snippet: Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth and his staff were publicly called out by an Army guard for violating decorum at Arlington National Cemetery following a Veterans Day service.
content:
WASHINGTON — Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and members of his inner circle received a public rebuke from an Army sentinel at Arlington National Cemetery on Wednesday following a Veterans Day ceremony attended by top administration officials.

Video footage showed Hegseth, alongside his wife Jennifer and key aides—including Chief of Staff Ricky Buria, Deputy Chief of Staff Patrick Weaver, and Senior Adviser Tami Radabaugh—posing for photographs on the steps of the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. As the group dispersed after taking photos, loud laughter broke out, prompting the on-duty tomb guard to loudly shout, "All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times."

A Standard of Silence at Hallowed Ground

The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier is widely regarded as one of the most sacred military sites in the nation, housing the remains of unidentified service members from World War I, World War II, and the Korean War. The memorial has been guarded continuously, 24 hours a day, by elite soldiers from the Army’s 3rd Infantry Regiment, known as "The Old Guard," since 1948.

Addressing the incident, top Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell praised the sentinel's intervention. "While commemorating this solemn day, a soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum," Parnell said in a statement, adding that Hegseth and the Department of Defense remain committed to honoring military sacrifices.

Political Fallout Amid Ongoing Tension

The encounter occurred just a day after Hegseth narrowly survived an impeachment effort in Congress spearheaded by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) and backed by Democrats. While the effort failed to remove Hegseth, critics are expected to revisit the issue when Democrats take control of Congress in January.

Hegseth had previously blasted the impeachment effort during a press conference, framing criticisms of his leadership as an attack on military members themselves and calling the resolution "sabotage." However, Wednesday's lapse in protocol drew fresh criticism from lawmakers. Rep. Gwen Moore (D-Wis.) posted on social media that Hegseth demonstrated an "utter lack of fitness for his office" by disrespecting the sanctity of the tomb.

The incident also revived memories of previous friction at Arlington National Cemetery, including a 2024 campaign event where Trump staff members clashed with cemetery personnel over federal regulations prohibiting political activities on sacred military grounds.
